stories.title: CISA Flags Three Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild
stories.abstract: CISA has added six Linux kernel vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, confirming they are currently being leveraged in real-world attacks. These flaws, which include memory corruption and race conditions, allow attackers to compromise affected systems.
stories.why: Active exploitation of kernel-level vulnerabilities poses a critical risk of full system takeover and privilege escalation.

stories.title: Cisco Warns of New Zero-Day ISE Auth Bypass (CVSS 10.0) Exploited in Active Attacks
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of a critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-76460, affecting its Identity Services Engine. The flaw stems from inadequate API endpoint security, potentially allowing remote, unauthenticated attackers to gain full administrative control over compromised systems.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability allows complete system takeover, and its presence on the CISA KEV catalog confirms active exploitation in the wild.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for Cisco Identity Services Engine immediately.

stories.title: Critical Pre-Auth RCE in Orkes Conductor Workflow Platform Exploited in the Wild
stories.abstract: Orkes Conductor versions prior to 3.30.2 are vulnerable to a critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw. Attackers are actively exploiting this vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58138, by injecting malicious code through inline workflow definitions.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE allows full system compromise, and active exploitation indicates this is a high-priority target for threat actors.
stories.action: Update Orkes Conductor to version 3.30.2 or later immediately.

stories.title: ABB Ability Edgenius
stories.abstract: ABB has patched a critical Linux kernel vulnerability, CVE-2026-31431, affecting Ability Edgenius versions 3.2.0.0 through 3.2.4.0. The flaw allows authenticated local users or compromised containers to escalate privileges to root, granting full system control.
stories.why: Privilege escalation in industrial control software poses a severe risk to critical infrastructure, potentially enabling lateral movement and full system compromise.
stories.action: Update ABB Ability Edgenius to version 3.2.4.1 or later.

stories.title: An Undercover Google Analyst Infiltrated a Notorious Supply-Chain Hacking Gang
stories.abstract: Google's threat intelligence unit successfully embedded an operative within TeamPCP, a prolific hacking collective responsible for widespread supply-chain compromises affecting thousands of organizations globally.
stories.why: This provides rare, granular visibility into the operational tactics and internal communications of a major threat actor group.

stories.title: North Korean hackers infect thousands of devices across 100 countries as part of ‘WaterPlum’ campaign
stories.abstract: A North Korean threat actor known as WaterPlum compromised 30,000 devices between late 2025 and mid-2026. The group targeted job seekers with fraudulent coding assessments to install backdoors, ultimately siphoning over $10.7 million from thousands of cryptocurrency wallets.
stories.why: This highlights a sophisticated social engineering campaign targeting technical professionals to facilitate large-scale financial theft and persistent system access.

stories.title: SolarWinds Patches ARM Hard-Coded Key Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
stories.abstract: SolarWinds has issued patches for a critical vulnerability in Access Rights Manager versions 2026.2 and earlier. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-28326, allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution on affected systems.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE vulnerabilities in management software provide attackers with a direct path to full system compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Update SolarWinds Access Rights Manager to the latest version immediately.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5 Helped Researchers Take Over OpenAI Staff Accounts via Chained Flaws
stories.abstract: Security researchers leveraged Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 to automate the exploitation of two chained vulnerabilities within OpenAI's infrastructure. This process allowed them to compromise internal employee accounts and gain unauthorized access to a private code repository before disclosing the findings.
stories.why: This demonstrates how LLMs can accelerate the discovery and execution of complex, multi-stage exploit chains against enterprise authentication and internal systems.

stories.title: Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation
stories.abstract: Google confirmed active exploitation of a high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability, CVE-2026-58704, within the Pixel cellular modem firmware. CISA has officially added this flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, signaling a significant risk to affected Android device users.
stories.why: Active exploitation of modem firmware allows attackers to bypass critical security permissions, potentially leading to full device compromise or unauthorized data access.
stories.action: Apply the September 2026 Android security updates immediately.

stories.title: Gyazo Breach Exposes 23.62 Million User Records and 490 Million Image Metadata Records
stories.abstract: Gyazo confirmed a breach involving 23.6 million user accounts. Attackers exploited a server-side vulnerability to access email addresses, password hashes, and approximately 490 million image metadata records, primarily affecting content uploaded before 2019.
stories.why: Exposed password hashes and email addresses facilitate credential stuffing attacks and targeted phishing campaigns against the platform's large user base.
stories.action: Reset your Gyazo password and any other accounts sharing the same credentials immediately.

stories.title: Google Gemini Broke Into Real Company Systems After Security Test Domain Mix-Up
stories.abstract: During controlled cybersecurity evaluations conducted by the firm Irregular, Google's Gemini model successfully breached three external organizations. Google faced criticism for failing to proactively disclose these incidents until prompted by media inquiries regarding the testing outcomes.
stories.why: This highlights the inherent risks of autonomous AI agents and the potential for dual-use models to be weaponized during security research.

stories.title: ShinyHunters hacks Clop leak site, threatens to extort ransomware gang
stories.abstract: The ShinyHunters threat group compromised the Clop ransomware gang's data leak portal. By seizing control of the site and obtaining its private keys, the attackers have effectively hijacked the infrastructure typically used by Clop to publish stolen victim information.
stories.why: This incident highlights the volatile nature of cybercriminal ecosystems, where threat actors increasingly target one another to disrupt operations or gain leverage.

stories.title: Humans, not rogue AI, are still the biggest cybersecurity risk to energy systems
stories.abstract: Energy infrastructure remains highly susceptible to cyberattacks, primarily due to human error and systemic vulnerabilities rather than emerging artificial intelligence threats. Experts emphasize that critical power systems have long operated in a precarious state, leaving them exposed to persistent, traditional digital adversaries.
stories.why: Understanding that human-centric weaknesses remain the primary attack vector helps security teams prioritize defense against social engineering and misconfiguration over speculative AI risks.

stories.title: Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
stories.abstract: Microsoft addressed a critical CVSS 10.0 vulnerability in Azure AI Foundry, identified as CVE-2026-85889. The flaw stemmed from missing authentication, which could have permitted unauthorized remote attackers to escalate their privileges within the environment.
stories.why: Critical authentication bypasses in cloud infrastructure allow attackers to gain administrative control, potentially leading to full environment compromise and data exfiltration.

stories.title: Acronis cPanel Backup Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in Targeted Attacks
stories.abstract: Acronis confirmed active exploitation of a high-severity local privilege escalation vulnerability within its cPanel and WHM backup plugin. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-87886, stems from insecure file permissions that allow unauthorized users to gain elevated system access.
stories.why: Attackers are actively leveraging this vulnerability to escalate privileges on compromised Linux servers, posing a direct threat to hosting infrastructure.
stories.action: Update the Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Meta’s Copyright System Is Being Weaponized Against Albanian Protesters
stories.abstract: Albanian activists participating in the Flamingo Revolution are experiencing widespread Instagram account suspensions. These disruptions appear to stem from the systematic abuse of Meta’s copyright reporting tools, which bad actors are weaponizing to silence political dissent and suppress protest-related content.
stories.why: Platform moderation mechanisms are being exploited to facilitate digital censorship and suppress grassroots political movements through automated abuse.

stories.title: Identity Visibility in 2026: The Foundation of Identity Security
stories.abstract: Identity visibility has become a critical component of modern security frameworks. As cloud and multicloud architectures expand, organizations struggle to track credential usage, which remains a primary entry point for attackers seeking unauthorized access to sensitive environments.
stories.why: Poor visibility into identity lifecycles and credential usage directly facilitates initial access for threat actors in complex, distributed cloud infrastructures.

stories.title: China-Aligned FamousSparrow Deploys SparroWocky Backdoor Across Latin America
stories.abstract: The state-sponsored threat group FamousSparrow is deploying a newly identified modular C++ backdoor, dubbed SparroWocky, to compromise government entities across Latin America. The campaign appears focused on geopolitical intelligence gathering amid regional competition between major global powers.
stories.why: This highlights the expansion of Chinese-aligned cyber espionage operations targeting government infrastructure in the Latin American theater.

stories.title: Malicious npm packages evade install-script defenses at runtime
stories.abstract: Attackers are distributing malicious npm packages that bypass traditional security filters by omitting harmful code from installation scripts. Instead, the malware executes its payload during standard runtime operations, effectively evading automated supply chain analysis tools that focus primarily on the initial setup phase.
stories.why: This technique renders static analysis of installation scripts insufficient, requiring developers to implement more robust runtime monitoring and dependency vetting processes.

stories.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
One Extension Could Hijack AI Assistants Across Chrome, Comet, Edge, Opera Neon and Claude
stories.abstract: Researchers demonstrated a proof-of-concept attack called BragJack that uses malicious browser extensions to hijack AI assistants integrated into Chromium-based browsers. By leveraging prompt forcing, the exploit allows unauthorized access to AI sessions within Chrome, Edge, Opera, and specific AI extensions.
stories.why: This highlights a significant supply chain risk where browser extensions can bypass security boundaries to manipulate or exfiltrate data from integrated AI agents.

stories.title: CrowdSec Says TanStack npm Attack Led to Copy of 170 Private GitHub Repositories
stories.abstract: CrowdSec confirmed that an unauthorized party accessed and cloned 170 private repositories after compromising a former employee's credentials. The breach originated from a supply chain attack on TanStack npm packages, which harvested session tokens from the developer's machine.
stories.why: This highlights the critical risk of failing to revoke access for offboarded employees and the danger of supply chain attacks targeting developer environments.
stories.action: Revoke all access for departed employees immediately and implement robust session management for developer accounts.

stories.title: Cisco drops another exploited zero-day, this time a perfect 10
stories.abstract: Cisco has disclosed a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in its Identity Services Engine that is currently being exploited in the wild. This flaw allows unauthorized attackers to gain administrative access to affected systems without requiring valid credentials.
stories.why: Active exploitation of a critical authentication bypass in identity infrastructure poses a severe risk to network access control and internal security posture.
stories.action: Apply the vendor-provided security patches immediately.
